Draw a network with pie-chart vertex marginal group probabilities

plot_marginals.Rd

Base-R visualization of posterior vertex marginal group memberships, drawing a pie chart at each vertex proportional to its marginal probabilities across aligned groups (the R equivalent of graph-tool's vertex_shape="pie" marginal plots).

Usage

plot_marginals(graph, mode, positions = NULL, radius = 0.04,
  palette = NULL, edge_col = grDevices::adjustcolor("grey40", 0.35),
  border = "grey20", labels = NULL, label_cex = 0.65, main = NULL, ...)

Arguments

graph

A graph created by graph_create.

mode

A rgraphtool_partition_mode from partition_mode_state or mode_cluster_state, or an \(N \times B\) numeric matrix of marginal counts or probabilities.

positions

Optional \(N \times 2\) matrix of vertex coordinates. When NULL, computes a deterministic spring layout initialized from the consensus partition.

radius

Pie-chart radius in normalized plot coordinates.

palette

Optional vector of group colours.

edge_col

Edge colour.

border

Pie slice border colour.

labels

Optional character vector of vertex labels.

label_cex

Character expansion for labels.

main

Optional plot title.

...

Additional arguments passed to graphics::plot.window().

Value

Invisibly, a list with normalized vertex positions, the marginal probabilities matrix, and the group colour palette.

See also

partition_mode_state, plot_hierarchy, demo("posterior_sampling")

Examples

g <- graph_create(6, directed = FALSE)
graph_add_edges(g, rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3), c(1, 3), c(4, 5), c(5, 6), c(4, 6), c(3, 4)))
pm <- partition_mode_state(list(c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2), c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2)))
plot_marginals(g, pm, main = "Vertex marginals")
